budget_items.what_was_said: The board discussed appropriating money now, ahead of a July 1 billing-company switch, to buy two radio data collectors so they are running before the transition. Figures for the cost were given inconsistently in the captions.

A commissioner clarified the cost is the fee to acquire and install the collectors, separate from the operational/billing part that would be in next year's budget; money would be pulled from a reserve.
The board discussed replacing aging excavation equipment (a 1996 tractor and 2008/2009 machines); pricing for a rubber-tired excavator was cited, with attachments adding to the cost.
A commissioner said the new equipment purchase could be funded from surplus, the same source the PFAS-related money had gone into, to be used on water line and plant work.

A commissioner asked how much the district currently budgets each year for main replacement; the figure given was described as the current annual allocation, which barely covers engineering when using outside contractors.

budget_items.topic: Rolling Acres in-house repair cost vs. contracted work
budget_items.what_was_said: Doing the Rolling Acres main replacement in-house was said to have cost a fraction of what a contracted job of that scope would have cost, illustrating the savings of in-house work.

budget_items.topic: Water rate impact of Massachusetts Avenue main project
budget_items.what_was_said: A resident noted his quarterly water bill rose by a stated amount after the Massachusetts Avenue main project and asked whether that increase applied to all customers.

decisions.decision: Two items (data collectors and new excavator/equipment) plus an IRS bill were settled as special-meeting articles; a well-testing/"Keings" article was set aside for the annual meeting instead, since it was seen as more controversial.
The special town meeting was set for Wednesday, February 25, 2026 at 6:00 p.m., timed to coincide with a regular commissioners' meeting.

The legal letter concerning a kayak rack in zone one (from an attorney named McGregor/on behalf of a Nathaniel Stevens) will be referred to the district's own attorney to respond, since it was addressed to the attorney.
The public engagement survey will be mailed to residents the last week of January, accompanied by a flyer with a QR code and a story in the Lunenburg Ledger.
The district will transition staff email addresses from the old Verizon.net address to new .gov addresses.
The district plans to move to a new analog radio alert system so crews are notified of a broken water main independent of cell phones.

minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Water District Commissioners set a special town meeting for February 25, 2026 to fund two data collectors, a new excavator, and an IRS bill, deferring a more contested well-testing article to the annual meeting. Most of the rest of the meeting covered PFAS treatment compliance deadlines, aging pipe infrastructure and in-house repair savings, a public engagement survey going out in late January, and a recent main break, closing with a vote to adjourn into executive session.

what_happened.line: Commissioners set a special town meeting for February 25, 2026 at 6:00 p.m., timed with a regular commissioners' meeting.

New data collectors for meter reading, a new excavator, and an IRS bill were settled as the special-meeting articles, while a more contested well-testing article was set aside for the annual meeting instead.
Commissioners said the data collectors and excavator would be funded from a reserve and from surplus, not described as new taxation.
A public engagement survey will be mailed to residents the last week of January, with a flyer, a QR code, and coverage in the Lunenburg Ledger.
The district plans a new radio alert system so crews learn of a broken water main independent of cell phones, after a recent Northfield Road main break.

why_it_matters: Residents will be asked at the February 25 special town meeting to fund an excavator, new meter-reading equipment, and an IRS bill; a separate well-testing question was moved to the annual meeting instead.
Public comment raised aging pipe infrastructure and PFAS treatment compliance deadlines as unresolved cost pressures that could affect future water rates and capital planning.
A resident's water bill increase after a recent main project was raised in public comment without a clear answer on whether it applies district-wide.
